text: A man who possesses that great art of pleasing universally, and of gaining the affections of those with whom he converses, possesses a strength which nothing else can give him: a strength which facilitates and helps his rise; and which, in case of accidents, breaks his fall.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CLXXXI, to his son, Bath, November 11, Old Style 1752
